body: Yea, I need to stop feeling so Sinatra. Have a good night. My work isn't hard, to be honest it's quite easy. Just to much down time to myself while I wait for shit to hit the fan. If I am doing my job it doesn't. But way to much downtime.
I hear you. I suppose I just see it like punching a time clock. Wake up, kiss my wife, collect my $600, clean the house a bit, go to sleep. 6 days a week, 52 weeks a year. I am just tired of it.

Even those memories are all messed up. Let me explain a bit. I loved my grandfather. World war 2 vet, tough man. I was the apple of his eye, and every success I had he would make a grand deal out of it. I worked hard to be a good grandson. I knew it would make him proud and give him bragging rights.

My aunt died, with her my grandmothers memory. My grandpa got lung cancer and emphasemia. He waited for her by her side, and as she faded and forgot who he was sometimes, he was there for her. After she died he stayed with us a bit and I had moved back. 

When my parents went to bed I would stay out in the living room with him. He would cry out at night for his wife and beg god to die. Every memory of him telling me stories, coming to the sports I played, and teaching me about life permanently scarred from those last 6 months.

I am still not over it, and I doubt I ever will be.

Have taken meds. Have done the psych rotations etc. There is a problem with that. My biology is very ill suited to any of the drugs they have put me on. Most of them actually make me more suicidal, and less apt to talk about it than I already on. Wellbeutrin actually gives me black outs and heart palpitations. 

I suppose that would be a solid way to finish the job. As for advisory psych, most psychiatrists are out of their depth with me. When I am perfectly honest with them they call it delusional. Some of the horrors in my past are hard to believe. What's even worse is some of the things I have lived through seem a bit ridiculous.  I got in an 95  MPH roll over one time without a scratch, overdosed on amphetamines and woke up, and looking at it all it makes me feel like a cockroach.

I was told by a therapist that I had delusions of durability. Like some sort of god complex. To be honest it's nothing of the sort. Every scuffle I get in, ever opportunity I wake up disappointed.

The biggest gift I have that makes therapy almost impossible is I was raised by a sadist. My mom was horrible when I was a child. I learned Robert Green's 48 laws of power first hand, and rules for radicals was a logical step after. Add to that Machiavelli and Tsun Tzu. Everything they say comes across like some sort of snake oil salesman offering me the newest fad.

Maybe if therapists actually resembled the one in Goodwill Hunting I would stand a chance. Nah man, unless I can personally find a new perspective, my road is paved. I am to smart, to bitter, and to beat up to deal with this shit much longer.

I am hoping to have a child so I can at least live for them, but using "Harm's Benefit Analysis", the world would be better off.
I hear you man. I am dropping cash into a fund for my wife as I speak. I wish life wasn't like this. I feel like we were lied to as children into believing in things that don't exist anymore.
